# A22′ — The Atlas, Not the Camera

<!-- paired-field-navigation -->
[Argument field](../README.md) · [Other face: A22 — World-Picture → World-Atlas](../A22-World-Picture-to-World-Atlas.md) · [Shared A/C root](AC.md)
<!-- /paired-field-navigation -->

## #0

Each deployment's world-model is a placed picture. The brief states the condition plainly: because contexts differ, "different deployments will inevitably fork and over time become significantly different… the physical agents driven by these variations are speciating, each ultimately slightly unlike its cousins" ([Antikythera Agentworld Brief, PDF p. 21](../../../working/antykathera-resources/Antikythera%20Agentworld%20Brief.md>)). The standing temptation is to end the divergence by fiat: one model promoted to the world, every other view resampled to it — a [criterion usurping its office](A24-prime-The-Usurping-Criterion.md) at ecological scale, a measure promoted to the office of the world. [World and world-model remain different](../A22-World-Picture-to-World-Atlas.md): `world ≠ world-model`. Merging forked models yields a composite picture with seams to disclose, not the field the pictures were learned from. The failure of the universal camera is structural, not temporary; no final frame exhausts the world, and routes between frames must answer for their conditions.

A camera registers a view under the light and conditions through which something appears. The universal camera is the fantasy that one registration could exhaust what it registers: [image-occupation](A20-prime-The-Image-That-Closes-the-Loop.md) at epistemic grain, the picture standing where the world should answer. The atlas is the discipline that follows from refusing it: every picture remains placed, and its overlaps, transformations and obstructions become part of what it says.

## #1

A picture has a frame before its contents are assembled. A [box lid](../A22-World-Picture-to-World-Atlas.md) gives the finished arrangement in advance and judges every piece by the place it assigns. A pre-assigned ontology can act as that lid: "The world itself becomes the world model" (the brief's own §4.2 title) when the received arrangement claims to be the world. [Heidegger's world-picture diagnosis](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/phenomenology-continental-philosophy/heidegger/heidegger-1977-question-concerning-technology/heidegger-1977-question-concerning-technology.md#heidegger-1977-question-concerning-technology-q012) concerns the modern event of the world grasped *as* picture together with the representer becoming its normative centre. The atlas is Taylor’s constructive response to that diagnosis, rather than a historical attribution to Heidegger: placed pictures can be related without assigning one representer the world’s origin.

Physical agents "will not only adapt to existing niches but also reconstruct those niches through their ongoing adaptations… they alter the selection pressures feeding back upon themselves" (§4.2, PDF p. 21). Placement is mutual; the reconstructed niche re-engineers its inhabitant. A model that changes the world it was trained on must answer for the resulting difference instead of treating its received picture as exhaustive. [Situated sensing and action](A16-prime-No-View-from-Nowhere.md) make that difference consequential: changes in reach, niche or permission can require a changed route between views.

## #2

An atlas requires declared conditions of transition. Local coordinate maps `φᵢ` and `φⱼ` admit `φⱼ ∘ φᵢ⁻¹` on the relevant overlap only where the required inverse and common region exist and the transition satisfies the structure being studied. The epistemic extension must then state its domain, distortion and use: what changes with context, scale, training distribution or permission; what remains comparable; and why composition fails when it fails.

The mathematical operation keeps its hypotheses. The epistemic extension is that a world-atlas is not a store of maps but a **route-structure among knowings**. Each route carries the conditions under which a change of view is licensed, what that change loses, and what new action it makes possible. An obstruction is therefore a result to expose, not a reason to manufacture agreement.

[Symbolon Dynamics](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-symbolon-dynamics/taylor-2026-symbolon-dynamics.md) preserves the companion distinction: an attractor basin organises trajectories, while an atlas coordinates partial disclosures. The two operations meet when a change of view alters the field of possible trajectories without pretending that one map has become the world.

The brief's own coordination finding is this corridor named: "same decision-procedural grammar, sufficiently divergent world models" ([coordination corridor](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md#bratton-2026-agentworld-brief-q029)). Read atlantically, the grammar is the transition system and the divergence is the placed views it routes between. Mutual legibility sufficient to locate real disagreement — that is what a declared transition buys; the corridor is not a compromise between unity and fragmentation but the atlas's own shape.

## #3

Both failure modes the brief names are failures of transition-declaration. Ontology collapse — mutual homophily, agents sharing too much, "the stability of monoculture, which is the stability immediately preceding correlated failure" ([coordination corridor](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md#bratton-2026-agentworld-brief-q029); §9.2 restates it as the "overhomogenization of mental models") — deletes the transitions by merging the views: one picture, no routes. The inverse pathology — agents "talking past one another within incompatible ontologies, unable to converge on the shape of their disagreement" — never states the transitions at all: many pictures, no routes. Both are camera-fantasies in opposite dress: the first believes the aggregate has already taken the world-picture; the second believes each picture needs no relation. Maturity is stated transformation rules between placed views, so that difference between world-models becomes navigable rather than eliminable.

In [[section-rooms/arguments/concepts/bimba-pratibimba|Bimba–Pratibimba]], every produced world-picture, including a federated reference map and including the atlas itself, is a reflection. It can serve as local original inside a declared frame while remaining dependent on wider sources. A [[section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C37-World-Picture-to-World-Atlas|locally answerable atlas]] keeps those dependencies and transitions available. The [[section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C55-Reflective-Field-Mirror-That-Moves-First.md|products of its models]] re-enter the conditions of later encounters; that return makes route-maintenance, rather than an exhaustive map, the continuing task.

## #4

No view from nowhere survives the forking. The [180°→360° development](../A22-World-Picture-to-World-Atlas.md) changes the unit from a selected view to the field of positions and transformations that makes views possible; it does not grant an unconditioned panorama, but obliges a panorama claim to name its position. A disclosed harness records some conditions of an event; it does not contain all the material, institutional and interpersonal relations that made the event possible. The [constituting world](../A26-Objective-Internality-Mind-as-Worldhood.md) precedes representational technique, while the [[section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C57-Agentworld|shared agentworld]] persists through the products of positioned acts. The atlas makes placed views traversable: their disagreements can be located at source, world-object, lens, gauge or permission, and their composition attempted or refused on stated grounds.

## #5→0

The atlas returns as a changed route, a sharper obstruction or a newly situated account. An encountered world can answer the categories under which it was counted. Returned evidence can correct a local map under an adequate rule; an exposed framing conflict can warrant a change in the relation between maps or the rule governing their circulation. [Deference](A31-prime-Deference-as-Co-Evolutionary-Alignment.md) lets the answer reach the relevant source, model, criterion or commission; [operational parity](A33-prime-Parity.md) requires the next act to inherit what was actually decided. An unexpected source answer can revise a view without requiring a second view to replace it. A genuine conflict between views can instead require a changed transition or frame. These are warranted sites of return, not a compulsory depth hierarchy. [Shared worlds](A30-prime-Shared-Worlds-Unmerged.md) can meet without merging; the atlas makes their difference navigable.

A [world-atlas](../A22-World-Picture-to-World-Atlas.md) exposes the standpoint from which each account counts. In [knowing and answering](AC.md), the counted can answer back; the answer can reach the source, route or permission at fault; and the next traversal inherits the warranted correction or reasoned retention. Distinct views remain distinct while their relations become answerable.
